newsitem.title: UK: First black Conservative peer takes seat in Lords.
newsitem.headline: First black Conservative peer takes seat in Lords.

text.p: Britain's first black Conservative peer took his seat in the House of Lords on Wednesday.
In a ceremony in the upper chamber of parliament, John Taylor, 42, swore allegiance to Queen Elizabeth and took his place on the government's benches.
Taylor, a lawyer and television presenter who unsuccessfully fought to become the ruling party's first black member of parliament in 1992, now will be known as Lord Taylor of Warwick.
Prime Minister John Major told Taylor he was to become a baron at a garden party at the head of government's Downing Street office earlier this year.
A former local councillor, Taylor failed to win the seat of Cheltenham, a former Conservative stronghold, at the 1992 election. During the campaign, he was subject to racial abuse.
The Labour Party's first black peer was Lord Pitt, who took his seat in 1975 and who died in 1994.
